committeeQuestion.question: During a provider outage, how can staff distinguish an authorised recovery instruction from a convincing phishing message?
committeeQuestion.why: Microsoft observed messages that impersonated service-health notices and claimed held emails would be deleted unless recipients acted.
committeeQuestion.evidence: A timed exercise using the published incident channel and a simulated recovery request, showing how recipients verify the message and where they report uncertainty.

committeeQuestions.question: Where could customer credentials still be stored or logged in readable form?
committeeQuestions.why: The CNIL found plaintext customer passwords in one enforcement case; the finding does not establish the position at another firm.
committeeQuestions.evidence: A scoped inventory of authentication stores and logs, sample-based verification and a dated remediation decision for any plaintext finding.

committeeQuestions.question: Which clearing arrangements depend on outsourced risk-management activity, and when is prior permission needed?
committeeQuestions.why: The Bank of England’s near-final policy describes permissions for CCP outsourcing and is subject to final legislation.
committeeQuestions.evidence: A list of relevant CCP services and contracts, the applicable permission analysis and the owner of any unresolved legal interpretation.

judgement.title: A recovery message can become the next attack.
judgement.editorialAngle: Use an observed outage-themed phishing campaign to test whether recovery communications can be verified when staff are under pressure.
judgement.distinctFromPrevious: Edition 22 tested intervention timing for an agent and recovery from a shared provider outage. Edition 23 examines whether the messages used during recovery can themselves be authenticated.
judgement.observation: Microsoft says a high-volume campaign on 13 November used messages disguised as Microsoft 365 service-health notifications, claiming held emails would be deleted unless recipients acted. It assessed the activity as likely credential phishing but did not confirm credential capture or post-compromise activity.
judgement.executiveJudgement: An outage gives an attacker a credible pretext to send urgent instructions just when staff expect unusual messages. Microsoft’s observations do not show that any particular firm was compromised. The decision for a firm is whether its people can verify a recovery request through a channel that does not depend on trusting the message itself.
judgement.implication: Ask the incident communications owner to run one simulated provider-outage notice. Measure how many recipients use the published verification channel before acting, how long confirmation takes, and what happens when that channel is unavailable. Use the result to decide which recovery instructions need a clearer route.

weeklyReadout.heading: Can staff verify a recovery instruction during an outage?
steps: Choose a material provider outage scenario.
Send a simulated recovery notice to the relevant team.
Measure independent verification and the time to confirm.
Decide how staff should proceed if the verification channel is unavailable.

topSignals.title: Outage recovery messages can become a phishing lure
topSignals.label: Microsoft threat intelligence · observed campaign
topSignals.why: Microsoft reports a high-volume campaign impersonating Microsoft 365 service-health messages. It assesses the activity was likely credential phishing; its evidence did not confirm credential capture or later compromise.

topSignals.title: Model safeguards can be challenged through coordinated extraction
topSignals.label: OpenAI · provider account
topSignals.why: OpenAI describes layered defences against adversarial distillation, including request-level protection and investigations. These are the provider’s account of its controls, not independent evidence of their effectiveness.

topSignals.title: Plaintext passwords exposed a basic control failure
topSignals.label: CNIL · enforcement decision
topSignals.why: France’s CNIL fined an unnamed company €5 million after finding, among other issues, that customer passwords were stored in plaintext. The decision concerns that company, not the state of controls across financial services.
topSignals.source: Primary / Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés / 2026-11-18

topSignals.title: CFTC alleges a large investment scheme misrepresented trading
topSignals.label: CFTC · civil complaint
topSignals.why: The CFTC alleges that a group solicited over $550 million while claiming returns from leveraged foreign-exchange trading. The complaint is an allegation, not a finding of liability.
topSignals.source: Primary / US Commodity Futures Trading Commission / 2026-11-20

topSignals.title: CCP outsourcing permissions remain subject to final legislation
topSignals.label: Bank of England · near-final policy
topSignals.why: The Bank of England published a near-final policy on permissions for central counterparties, including outsourcing major risk-management activities. It remains subject to final Treasury legislation.
topSignals.source: Primary / Bank of England and Prudential Regulation Authority / 2026-11-16
